key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically extract many key breast oncology variables from long, messy charts with high agreement to expert abstraction.
clinical_relevance: If validated broadly, this approach could reduce the manual workload needed to build research cohorts and study outcomes from real-world cancer records.
method: Randomly sampled 100 patients from a complex breast cancer cohort
Compared 4 general-purpose LLMs against oncologist abstraction, genetic records, and some research coordinator abstraction
Used an open-source, HIPAA-compliant pipeline without fine-tuning or hand-picking notes
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the best models (GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro) reached 90%–100% concordance for several key variables, and a separate 97-patient cohort showed similar recurrence detection performance.
watch_item: Performance still needs replication across institutions and diseases, and therapy-line reconstruction was less accurate than expert review.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
